# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH COAGULASE-NEGATIVE STAPHYLOCOCCI (CoNS)

CoNS are normal commensal human skin flora and are not typically pathogenic.

However, they are the most common cause of health care associated blood stream

infections (30%). Unlike other commonly isolated CoNS, S. lugdunensis can cause

severe disease like S. aureus. Refer to Bacteremia Associated S. lugdunensis

recommendations for treatment.

[Bacteremia associated with Staphylococcus lugdunensis](staphylococcus-lugdunensis-bacteremia)

Other commonly isolated CoNS are S. epidermidis, S. haemolyticus, and S.

saprophyticus. In a patient without signs or symptoms of infection, a single

positive blood culture for these CoNS isolates often represents contamination

and not infection. CoNS are more likely to be pathogens in patients with a

prosthetic device. Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.

[Approach to Endocarditis](endocarditis-approach-to)

Treatment is indicated when there are more than 1 blood culture bottle is

positive for CoNS. Follow-up blood cultures should be obtained within 24-48

hours after initiating antimicrobial therapy. Identification and treatment of

the source of infection, in addition to antimicrobial therapy, is crucial for

resolution of infection. This may include removal of catheters and draining of

abscesses if present.

# Duration of therapy:

Treat for 7 - 14 days. A longer duration is required in metastatic infection.

Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.

# Treatment for methicillin-susceptible staphylococci (mecA negative)

Preferred:

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

Alternatives:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

# Treatment for methicillin-resistant staphylococci (mecA positive)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)
